contract: DELEGATED WORK ON A RENDERED GRID, frozen here so the Rust reader and the TypeScript reader
answer the SAME question about the SAME screens -- or fail together.
WHY THIS FIXTURE EXISTS. The founder's rule is 'DELEGATED WORK COUNTS AS ACTIVITY': an agent
that fans out must render GREEN both while it is working with subagents live and while it is
BLOCKED WAITING on them. The second state is the one that was missed, because from the parent's
own PTY it looks exactly like doing nothing -- no spinner, no output, no tool calls, for
minutes. The evidence that it is NOT doing nothing is on the grid, and two different languages
now read it: TypeScript for a MOUNTED pane (engine/backgroundTaskFooter.parseDelegatedWorkCount)
and Rust for every agent whether or not anyone has opened it
(observed_attention::delegated_work_visible).
AGENTS.md records what happens without a shared fixture, measured: two agents built the two
halves of a Rust->TS feature in parallel against a frozen field list, both suites passed, the
merge was clean, and the shipped feature never once ran. So both suites parse THIS file and
assert the same partition of the same screens.
DERIVE THE PARTITION, DO NOT RESTATE IT. Each screen carries `delegating`, and each suite must
compute its own answer and compare. A test that lists which screens are delegating and then
asserts that list is vacuous -- it passes with the matcher deleted. Both directions must red:
a matcher that stops recognising a delegating screen, AND one that starts recognising an idle
one.
TWO SURFACES, AND THEY ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE:
footer -- `N background task(s) live [ctrl+b to manage]`, work Claude has BACKGROUNDED. The
count must be strictly POSITIVE; `0 background tasks live` is not live work.
roster -- `<circle> <kind>  <label>  <elapsed>`, subagents running right now. This block
REPLACES the composer box, which is why a screen showing it has no other sign of
life on it at all.
BOTH SURFACES ARE POSITION-CHECKED, in both languages. Each is easy to QUOTE: this very file
reproduces a roster row and a footer verbatim, and so does the TypeScript reader's own header,
so a pager -- or a plain `cat` -- showing either document trips the pattern. Claude draws both
as the LAST thing on a live grid, so the last matching line must terminate it.
TERMINATES HAS TWO SHAPES, and requiring only the first is a NARROW-PANE BUG. A strictly
line-anchored walk rejects Claude's own status bar when Ink WRAPS it -- at 12 columns the bar
becomes three rows and only the first carries a glyph -- so a real pane with subagents running
answers `null`, the mounted reader forgets the count, and the row goes gray while its delegates
run. Both readers therefore accept EITHER the line-anchored walk OR a rejoined tail that OPENS
with one of Claude's own bar phrases. The anchor is what keeps a document out: a paragraph
about the footer opens with its own prose.
AND THE ANCHOR USES THE BAR GLYPHS ONLY, not the wider status-glyph class. That class contains
ordinary text bullets, and the permission-mode phrase is purely structural, so together they
would accept any tail opening with a bullet and a short run of letters ending in ` on` -- an
ordinary sentence. Where this gate is the SOLE reason a row turns green, and where the pane is
static so nothing can scroll the line away, that is a latch rather than a wrong guess.
AND THE WHOLE TAIL IS ACCOUNTED FOR, not only its opening. The anchor says where the rejoined
tail STARTS; everything after it was joined and never examined, so a document that opens with a
real bar and then keeps going cleared the gate. A wrapped bar is ONE logical line, so its
rejoined length is bounded by what a bar can be -- the longest captured from a real pane is 48
characters. A false negative here costs only the gray row that shipped for months.
NOTE WHAT THIS FILE DOES *NOT* GOVERN: whether it is safe to TYPE into a pane. That question
belongs to `isClaudeCodeScreen`, whose subagent-roster family keeps the strict line-anchored
walk. Colour and authorization have different costs -- a wrong colour is a wrong colour, a wrong
authorization is a line pasted and submitted into a pager -- so they must not share a threshold.
The footer was briefly exempted, on the argument that its wording is far less quotable than a
bullet row. The commit making that argument falsified it in the same breath by adding those
exact bytes to two files agents routinely read. Unchecked it is worse than a wrong answer, it
is a LATCH: the viewport is static, so nothing scrolls the line off, and the rows this feature
promotes are precisely the ones with no mounted writer to correct them.

FOUNDER STATE 2 -- blocked waiting on subagents. The roster, terminating the grid. This is the founder's own screenshot shape: no spinner, no output, nothing but the list.

screens.why: A roster of ONE, with trailing blank rows. Blanks are free below the list in both readers.

A REAL NARROW PANE. Claude's status bar WRAPS below the footer -- at 12 columns `  <pause> manual mode on . ? for shortcuts` renders as three rows and only the first carries a glyph, so a strictly line-anchored walk rejects it and the row goes GRAY with three subagents running. Both readers rejoin the tail and require the JOIN to open with one of Claude's own bar phrases, which a document's tail does not.

A NARROW PANE SHOWING ONLY THE ROSTER. Same pane, same width, same wrapped status bar -- and a roster commonly appears with NO footer under it to fall back on, so the roster arm needs the identical accommodation the footer arm got. Without it a row goes GRAY with its subagents visibly listed on the grid.

A DOCUMENT WHOSE TAIL OPENS WITH A TEXT BULLET. `all tests pass on main` is ordinary prose, but a bullet plus <=29 letters ending in ` on` satisfies a structural permission-mode bar -- so anchoring on the WIDE status-glyph class would clear this and latch the row green. The anchor uses the BAR glyphs only.

A DOCUMENT THAT OPENS ITS TAIL WITH A REAL BAR AND KEEPS GOING. The anchor constrains where the rejoined tail STARTS; without a length bound everything after it is joined and never examined, so this cleared the gate. Not hypothetical -- this branch's own commit messages reproduce a wrapped bar verbatim.

Unchecked it is a LATCH: the viewport is static, no prompt is present, and the promoted row has no mounted writer to correct it. Position is the discriminator for BOTH surfaces.
